description: Change what a structured database already holds. action: update_rows (`database_id`, `table`, `updates`: [{_id, values}] — get _id values from `query`) | delete_rows (`database_id`, `table`, `row_ids`) | update_view (`database_id`, `table`, `view` = view_id or name, plus the view fields to change; `name` renames it). Column types: text, number, checkbox (0/1), date (YYYY-MM-DD), single_select, files (links to files stored with the database, one per line; `media_upload` with the database's id stores one and returns its link). `table` accepts a table_id, a physical name, or a display name. A view is a saved way of looking at a table that everyone sees, like a Notion view: optional `filter`, `sorts`, `group_by`, `hidden_columns` and `kind`. A filter is one condition {column_id, op, value} (op: contains|not_contains|eq|ne|gt|gte|lt|lte|empty|not_empty) or a group {and: [...]} / {or: [...]} of them; column references accept a column_id, physical name or display name. Changes are PROPOSED, never applied blindly: by default the tool returns `Proposed` and your change waits for the user to accept it — that is SUCCESS, never retry it. They are notified. The owner may instead have set the item to let AI edits apply directly, and then the result says `Applied`; or to be reviewed by a colleague, so someone other than the user accepts it. `revises`: the ids of the CHANGES REQUESTED this proposal answers (from the block your reads open with); until a proposal names them, they keep leading your reads. ONE piece of work is ONE change, reviewed on one card: an ingest of a meeting or an email, or one Save to Stuga of several points. Give `change_title` (a few words naming its source, never a page's title) to your FIRST write for it, and pass the `change_id` the answer returns to EVERY later write for it, on every page and database; `change_summary` says what it does. A new page made inside a change, where AI edits wait for a colleague, stays visible only to the user and those who may approve it until it is approved. When your earlier change to a page is still undecided, a write there for another change waits behind it in a queue (`queued_behind`): that is SUCCESS, never retry it.

change_id.description: The `change_id` your first write for this piece of work returned: pass it to every later write for it.

change_summary.description: What the change does, in a sentence or two, for whoever approves it; a later write may replace it.

change_title.description: Opens a change for this piece of work and returns its `change_id`: a few words naming its source, as "Customer sync, 2026-10-21".

workspace_id.description: The workspace to act in: a `workspace_id` from `workspaces` action:list, which also says which node it is on.
